earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: retired 2014 as duplicate of Romam [rmx], bookkeeping-only entry. No Lamam description exists.

sources.citation: SEAlang SALA full-text index (sealang.net/sala), whole-word searches 'Romam', 'Lamam', 'Kachok', 'Kaco', 'Ramam' (run 2026-09-17).
sources.note: Only passing mentions: Bui Khang The 1996 (Romam population ~200-300); 'Lamam' as a Xekong (Laos) district name in Theraphan 1997, 2002; in a language-name list in Ferlus 1996; Williams & Hoonchamlong 1996 quoting Wurm & Hattori 1981 atlas 'LAMAM 1000'. No description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lexibank CLLD entry 'Ramam' (sidwellbahnaric-ramam): Sidwell, Paul. 2024. CLDF dataset derived from the Bahnaric data in Sidwell's 'Austroasiatic dataset for phylogenetic analysis' (2015). Zenodo.
sources.note: Wordlist with segment inventory only; no prosodic information.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2021. Change Request Number 2021-018: adopted update [xkk] (additional name Kachok; effective 2022-01-20). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; name-spelling change only. Mentions 'a recent dissertation writes Kachok' (unidentified) and 'Linguist Bong Sok who works with this language group'.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2013. Change Request Number 2013-028: adopted merge [lmm] -> [rmx] Romam (effective 2014-02-03). Submitted by Eric Pawley (SIL/ICC Phnom Penh). Dallas: SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. States only: 'There is no Lamam language in Cambodia.. there is already a Romam language in Vietnam.. confined to one village, numbering between 200-400 people in Le village, Mo Rai commune, Sa Thay district of Kon Tum province.'

sources.citation: Magaspag, Chitse E. 2012. Language Use and Attitudes of Kachok Speakers: Towards an Assessment of the Kachok Language Vitality. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-038. Dallas: SIL International. 261 pp. (publication of 2009 Philippine Normal University MA thesis).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (sociolinguistic survey; no phonology). Relevant for identity: pp. 58, 115-116 report that 'Lamam' (informal) = 'Romam' (formal) is a Kachok clan name and that the Lamam on the Vietnam border 'are Kachok'; pp. 49, 127: the only Kachok documentation is unpublished wordlists (Diffloth 2001; Diffloth & Gregerson 2003; ICC survey 2006).

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A., Kenneth J. Gregerson & Paul Sidwell. 2011. The North Bahnaric clade: a computational approach. In Srichampa, Sidwell & Gregerson (eds.), Austroasiatic Studies: papers from ICAAL4, Mon-Khmer Studies Special Issue No. 3, 33-47. Dallas: SIL / Salaya: Mahidol / Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Ramam/Rmam appears only as a lexical-phylogeny taxon, sister of Kacho: 'Kacho and Ramam seem to show the same or similar vowel history to Rengao.. reduced by a later independent general devoicing of stops in Kacho/Ramam' (p. 34); 'speakers of their sister dialect Ramam in a small community of just a few hundred on the Vietnam side of the border' (p. 35). Data source listed as unpublished 'Roman [sic] list 2007'.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Kaco' language' (Romam_language redirects there) and Wikipedia (vi) 'Tiếng Rơ Măm', 'Người Rơ Măm'; VJOL (Vietnam Journals Online) search 'Rơ Măm'.
sources.note: Nothing. en-wiki: 'Lamam (Lmam) is a clan name found among the Kaco', not a distinct language'; sources cited are Ethnologue, Đặng et al. 2010 (ethnographic handbook) and Magaspag 2012. VJOL returns only ethnographic/genetic articles on the Rơ-măm, no linguistic description.

sources.citation: 'Roman [Romam] list 2007' -- unpublished Romam wordlist used as the Rmam taxon in Edmondson, Gregerson & Sidwell 2011 ('full details or images supplied on request'); underlying data also in Sidwell 2015 Austroasiatic phylogenetic dataset (Lexibank sidwellbahnaric 'Ramam').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only known primary Romam data; a transcribed wordlist might mark stress or presyllable reduction, but it is unpublished.

sources.citation: Diffloth, Gérard & Kenneth Gregerson. 2003. Kachok wordlist (unpublished ms., elicited Andoung Meas district, Ratanakiri, 2001), cited in Magaspag 2012: 49, 127.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other primary lexical documentation of the Kachok/Lamam cluster; unpublished.

sources.citation: Ferlus, Michel. 1972. Notes sur les dialectes austroasiens du Sud Laos. Asie du Sud-Est et Monde Insulindien (ASEMI) 3(2): 35-49.

sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Glottolog's language code list for this article includes 'Lamam' -- the likely origin of the Lamam entry in Wurm & Hattori 1981 and Ethnologue; would clarify what 'Lamam' originally denoted (probably brief notes/wordlist, unlikely to state stress). Not on SEAlang SALA or HAL.

sources.citation: Unidentified 'recent dissertation' on Kachok referred to in ISO 639-3 CR 2021-018 (2021, submitted with input from 'linguist Bong Sok'); possibly a Kachok phonology/grammar thesis (SIL Cambodia / Payap or similar), which would be the first description of the Kacho-Ramam (Lamamic) pair.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only hint of a first-hand linguistic description of the Lamamic (Kacho/Romam) cluster; if it has a phonology chapter it would state stress placement for the sister dialect of Romam. sil.org behind an automated-access block).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid pages lama1290 (bookkeeping; iso_retirement 2013-028) and roma1331 Romam (refs: WRITENET 2002 'Vietnam: Indigenous Minority Groups in the Central Highlands' [overview]; Vu Dinh Loi 2001 'Brau and Romam cultures' [ethnographic]; Ethnologue 16; Glottolog's most extensive description = wordlist or less) + on-disk glottolog-cldf-5.1 sources.bib search for Romam/Lamam/Kachok.

sources.note: No descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference exists for either languoid; 'Lamam' otherwise occurs only in the language code list of Ferlus 1972 (ASEMI 3(2):35-49).
